catalog_quote: §3. Word and sentence prosody. Tonkawa utterances consist of a succession of more or less evenly stressed syllables. In no case does it appear that either stress or pitch accent plays any significant role in the word. sources.citation: Gouskova, Maria. 2003. Deriving Economy: Syncope in Optimality Theory. PhD dissertation, University of Massachusetts Amherst (317 pp).
sources.quote: Quotes Hoijer 1946:292 'Tonkawa utterances consist of a succession of more or less evenly stressed syllables'; fn.50 quotes verbatim the disyllable-final / polysyllable-penult sentence and conjectures the disyllable remark may reflect apocope words like notox 'hoe'; 'Hoijer's description of stress is not detailed enough to deduce whether Tonkawa has iambic or trochaic stress' (she infers trochaic footing from vowel shortening).

sources.citation: Wier, Thomas. 2015. Templatic Dependencies and Notions of Wordhood in Tonkawa. Ms., lingbuzz/002519 (18 pp).
sources.quote: Only says 'prosodic footing occurs from the right, not the left (Hoijer 1933: 21)' and quotes Hoijer 1933:22 'Neither syllabification nor accent seem to have ... any morphological distinctions entirely dependent upon them'; no independent stress-placement statement.
